records.text: Give ear, O heaven, and I will speak; and let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
Let my utterance be awaited as the rain, and let my words descend as the dew, as a shower upon the grass, and as snow upon the herbage.
For I have called upon the name of the Lord; ascribe greatness unto our God.
God—true are His works, and all His ways are judgments; a faithful God, and there is no unrighteousness; righteous and holy is the Lord.
Hear the Lord’s word, house of Jacob and every clan of the house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord: What offense did your fathers find in Me, that they withdrew far from Me, followed futile things and became futile?

They did not say, Where is the Lord who brought us up from Egypt’s land, who guided us in the wilderness, in a boundless and impassable land, a waterless and fruitless land, a land through which nothing passed and where no human being lived?
“I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

And God's Spirit came upon him, and he took up his parable and said: Balak summoned me from Mesopotamia, the king of Moab from the eastern mountains: Come, curse Jacob for me; come, call down a curse on Israel for me.
Why should I curse whom the Lord does not curse? Why should I call down a curse on whom God does not curse?
From the tops of mountains I shall see them, and from the hills I shall observe them. Behold, a people who will dwell alone, not counted among the nations.
Who has measured Jacob’s seed exactly, and who will count Israel's clans? May my soul die among righteous souls, and may my seed be like their seed!
And Balak said to Balaam: What have you done to me? I summoned you to curse my enemies, and look, you have pronounced a blessing!
And Balaam said to Balak: Must I not take care to speak what God puts in my mouth?
I will not rebuke you concerning your sacrifices; your burnt offerings are continually before Me.
I will not receive calves from your house or young goats from your flocks.
For all the forest’s wild animals are Mine, beasts on the mountains and cattle.
I know all the birds of heaven, and the field’s beauty is with Me.
If I become hungry, I will certainly not tell you, for the inhabited world and its fullness are Mine.
Will I eat bulls’ flesh or drink goats’ blood?
Sacrifice a sacrifice of praise to God and pay your vows to the Most High.
Call on Me in the day of affliction; I will rescue you, and you will glorify Me.” Diapsalma.
Samuel said, “Are whole burnt offerings and sacrifices as desirable to the Lord as listening to the Lord’s voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and attentiveness than the fat of rams.
Divination is sin; teraphim bring sorrow and troubles. Because you treated the Lord’s word as nothing, the Lord will treat you as nothing, so that you will not be king over Israel.”

And now, O Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, and to love Him, and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
to keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and His ordinances which I command you this day, that it may be well with you?

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, but have left aside the weightier matters of the Law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness! These you ought to have done without leaving those aside.
Blind guides, straining out the gnat but swallowing the camel!
The Lord is near to all who call on Him, to all who call on Him in truth.
He will fulfill the will of those who fear Him; He will hear their plea and save them.
The Lord guards all who love Him, and all sinners He will utterly destroy.
A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish son is grief to his mother.
Treasures will not profit lawless people, but righteousness will rescue from death.
The Lord will not starve a righteous life, but He will overturn the life of the impious.
You shall not have in your pouch differing weights, a great and a small.
You shall not have in your house differing measures, a great and a small.
You shall have a true and just weight, and you shall have a true and just measure, that your days may be long upon the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.
For everyone who does these things, everyone who does injustice, is an abomination unto the Lord your God.
For impious people were found among My people, and they set traps to destroy men and were catching them.
Like a set trap full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit; therefore they became great and rich.
And they transgressed judgment; they did not judge an orphan’s case, and they were not judging a widow’s case.
Shall I not visit for these things? says the Lord. Or will not My soul take vengeance on such a nation?
And I will bring upon you a sword exacting the penalty of the covenant. You shall flee into your cities, and I will send death among you; you shall be handed into enemies’ hands.
When I afflict you with a scarcity of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven and give back your bread by weight. You shall eat and in no wise be filled.
You shall carry much seed into the field, and gather little; for the locust shall devour it.
You shall plant a vineyard and dress it, but shall neither drink wine nor rejoice in it; for the worm shall devour it.
You shall have olive trees throughout all your borders, but shall not anoint yourself with oil; for your olives shall fall away.
Zimri, commander of half the cavalry, conspired against him. He was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Osa, the steward in Tirzah.
Zimri came in, struck him, put him to death, and reigned in his place.
When he became king, as soon as he sat on his throne, he struck down all Baasha’s house,
according to the word which the Lord spoke against Baasha’s house to Jehu the prophet,
concerning all the sins of Baasha and Elah his son, how he caused Israel to sin, provoking the Lord, the God of Israel, with their worthless things.
The rest of Elah’s acts and all he did—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah. Israel’s camp was against Gibbethon, which belonged to the foreigners.
The people in the camp heard it said, “Zimri has conspired and struck the king!” They made Omri, the army commander, king in Israel, over Israel, that day in the camp.
Omri and all Israel with him went up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.
When Zimri saw that his city had been taken, he went into a cave of the king’s house. He burned the king’s house over himself with fire and died,
because of the sins he committed, doing evil before the Lord, walking in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, as he caused Israel to sin.
The rest of Zimri’s acts and the conspiracies he formed—behold, are these not written in the Book of the Annals of the Kings of Israel?
In Jehoshaphat’s second year, Ahab son of Omri became king. He reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
Ahab did evil before the Lord; he acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
It was not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat: he took as wife Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and went and served Baal and bowed down to him.
He set up an altar for Baal in the house of his offenses which he had built in Samaria,
and Ahab made a grove. Ahab went on committing provocations, to provoke his soul to destruction; he did evil more than all the kings of Israel who had been before him.
